name: PostHog Android SDK

dataTypes.when: Always by default: captureApplicationLifecycleEvents (Application Installed/Updated/Opened/Backgrounded), captureScreenViews ($screen) and captureDeepLinks (Deep Link Opened) all default to true, plus any events you capture().

dataTypes.type: Device or other IDs / Device or other IDs
dataTypes.when: Always. The SDK generates a random anonymous ID (UUID) used as the distinct ID until identify() is called.

ask: Do you call PostHog.identify() with your own user ID? If yes, also declare Personal info / User IDs.

Do you pass person properties such as email or name to identify() (userProperties / userPropertiesSetOnce)? If yes, declare Personal info / Email address and/or Personal info / Name (and any other personal data you send).

Is session replay enabled (sessionReplay = true and 'Record user sessions' on in project settings)? It records the screen (wireframes by default; real screenshots if screenshot = true, which may contain sensitive content), and captures Logcat by default (captureLogcat = true). Text inputs and images are masked by default (maskAllTextInputs / maskAllImages = true). If enabled, declare App activity / App interactions and App info and performance / Diagnostics at least, and review whether unmasked screens show personal data, photos or messages.
Is error tracking autocapture enabled (errorTrackingConfig.autoCapture = true, default false)? If yes, declare App info and performance / Crash logs.
The fetched PostHog Android docs do not describe IP or GeoIP handling. If your PostHog project enriches events with GeoIP (city/country), declare Location / Approximate location.
notes: PostHog does not publish a Google Play Data safety guide for Android; entries are mapped from its SDK docs. No vendor statement on sharing was found; treated as a service provider (processes data on the developer's behalf). Self-hosted PostHog sends data to the developer's own server.
